Since the value set is closed (`application` / `resource` / `system`), modeling this as an enum would let weaver actually validate the emitted values instead of just accepting any string. At minimum, add `system` to the examples.

replies.body:
I've fixed that in 4ffb455 and it's now modeled as an enum.

However, it seems that the concept of "closed enum" [described here](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/how-to-write-conventions/#defining-enum-attribute-members) is not being enforced anymore by default, if we want that we need to add a custom rego policy.

This has been removed in weaver as described in this issue https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/issues/1247.

Also, all the usages of `allow_custom_values` in semantic conventions have been removed, as found in https://github.com/ollygarden/opentelemetry-agent-skills/pull/88 description all enums are "open by default".

So, this is a case where current metric assertions provide more exhaustive coverage of metric attribute values, which means weaver validation only complements the current testing strategy but might not replace it. Another aspect where it fails short is the lack of metric description check.
